Wind Financial Morning Post: August 21, 2026

Market Brief

China’s LPR remains unchanged for 15 consecutive months.

Shanghai introduces new real estate policies, lowering down payment ratio for second homes outside the outer ring to 15%.

Xu Jiayin sentenced to life imprisonment; first-instance verdict delivered in cases involving Evergrande Group, Evergrande Real Estate and others.

Trump announces “devastating economic actions” against Iran.

U.S. government advances cryptocurrency regulations, but key bill stalls in Congress.

U.S. Treasury Secretary Bessent says U.S. debt buybacks could be scaled up, with single transactions potentially exceeding $4 billion.

Global stock markets diverge on Thursday; U.S. equities weaken while South Korea’s KOSPI surges 5.89%.
Alibaba reports 9% revenue growth for first quarter of fiscal year 2027, accelerating AI commercialization.

Top Stories

Shanghai has optimized its real estate policies, primarily covering five areas and eight measures: optimizing housing provident fund withdrawals, optimizing personal housing credit, implementing housing “trade-in” subsidies, promoting housing voucher resettlement, and advancing the purchase of second-hand homes. After adjustment, the minimum down payment ratio for first-time homebuyers using commercial loans is uniformly set at 15%; for second homes, the minimum down payment ratio inside the outer ring is no less than 25%, and outside the outer ring (including all of Baoshan and Jiading districts) is no less than 15%; housing provident funds can be withdrawn to pay deed taxes or purchase parking spaces; maximum subsidy for “trade-in” is 80,000 yuan.

The first-instance verdict was handed down in the cases involving Evergrande Group, Evergrande Real Estate, and Xu Jiayin. The Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court imposed a combined fine of RMB 8.82 billion on Evergrande Group, a fine of RMB 7 billion on Evergrande Real Estate, and sentenced Xu Jiayin to life imprisonment, deprivation of political rights for life, and confiscation of all personal property for multiple offenses. Additionally, in relation to other individuals involved in Evergrande Group’s illegal absorption of public deposits, fundraising fraud, and unauthorized use of funds, the court lawfully sentenced 56 individuals, including Xu Tenghe and Xu Zhijian, to fixed-term imprisonment with fines or property confiscation.

Due to stalled negotiations with Iran, U.S. President Trump announced “devastating economic actions” against Iran. Trump declared that the United States would impose the most severe economic measures on Iran, constituting an unprecedented economic war and isolation campaign. Any country permitting its financial institutions, enterprises, airports, or government entities to support Iran will face “massive economic consequences.” Iran’s Foreign Minister Alireza Araghchi responded that this U.S. move aims to divert domestic attention from fiscal issues, including high debt levels and rising interest expenditures.
U.S. Treasury Secretary Bessent has issued a series of policy signals covering recent market hotspots such as the U.S. bond market and Iran-related issues. As yields on long-term U.S. Treasuries rebounded, Bessent stated that the Treasury’s single bond buyback could exceed $4 billion and emphasized that the Treasury possesses a robust policy toolbox. On Iran, Bessent revealed that a press conference will be held on August 24 to detail the U.S. action plan against Iran. The United States will impose the “strictest ever” sanctions on Iran, and if maximum economic pressure is applied, large-scale military action is unlikely to be necessary. Bessent reaffirmed the strong dollar policy, stating that the dollar is returning to levels seen two months ago.

China Macro & Policy

Swiss Federal Council President and Minister of Economic Affairs, Education and Research, Guy Parmelin, met with Chinese Minister of Commerce Wang Wentao in Bern, jointly announcing the completion of negotiations for the upgraded China-Switzerland Free Trade Agreement and the signing of a memorandum of understanding. In September 2024, China and Switzerland launched negotiations to upgrade the FTA. After five rounds of consultations, the upgrade negotiations were successfully concluded. Both sides pledged to pursue higher-level bilateral openness across multiple areas including goods, services, investment, and rules, creating new opportunities for economic and trade cooperation between the two countries.

The People’s Bank of China released the August LPR rates: the one-year LPR is 3.0% and the five-year-and-over LPR is 3.5%, both unchanged from July and remaining unchanged for 15 consecutive months. Wang Qing, Chief Macro Analyst at Oriental Jincheng, believes the PBOC may later implement policy rate cuts, which would lead to a corresponding LPR adjustment, with possible rate cuts and reserve requirement ratio reductions by the end of the third quarter.

Zheng Shanjie, Director of the National Development and Reform Commission, chaired a symposium with private enterprises to hear opinions and suggestions on stabilizing economic operations and promoting effective investment. The NDRC will next fully leverage the effectiveness of existing policies and promptly formulate practical and effective new policies.

The National Immigration Administration announced that, starting August 20, citizens of Kyrgyzstan and Vietnam are eligible for the 240-hour transit visa-free policy and the 30-day visa-free entry policy for Hainan. With this, the number of countries eligible for the 240-hour transit visa-free policy has increased to 57, and the number of countries eligible for the 30-day visa-free entry policy for Hainan has increased to 61.

The contribution of new drivers to China’s industrial economy continues to strengthen. From January to July, new driver sectors represented by high-tech manufacturing and digital product manufacturing accounted for approximately 50% of the growth in industrial value-added above designated size, an increase of about 3 percentage points from the first half of the year. Artificial intelligence has driven rapid growth in output of products such as sensors, memory chips, and optical fibers.

China Equities Markets

On Thursday, A-shares rebounded amid volatility, with the Shanghai Composite Index closing up 0.24% at 3,903.72 points, the Shenzhen Component Index rising 0.59%, the ChiNext Index gaining 0.64%, and the Wind All-A Index advancing 0.61%. Trading volume contracted to RMB 2.09 trillion. Shares in the pharmaceutical and biotechnology sector surged with a wave of limit-up gains, as vaccines, cellular immunotherapy, recombinant protein, and gene editing sub-sectors all performed strongly. Real estate and fiber-optic-related stocks also strengthened, while seed industry stocks retreated. Yushu Technology fell over 18% on its second trading day.

Hong Kong stocks rose amid volatility, with the Hang Seng Index closing up 0.8% at 25,698.49 points, the Hang Seng Tech Index gaining 0.39%, and the Hang Seng China Enterprises Index rising 0.9%. Net selling by southbound funds amounted to HKD 10.412 billion, while Alibaba recorded net buying of HKD 2.2 billion. The metals and mining, pharmaceutical and biotechnology, automotive, and real estate sectors led gains, while the semiconductor supply chain weakened.

Alibaba reported revenue of 268.95 billion yuan for the first quarter of fiscal year 2027, up 9% year-over-year; adjusted net profit was 20.72 billion yuan, down 38%. AI commercialization has accelerated significantly; Alibaba Cloud revenue increased 45% year-over-year, with AI-related product revenue reaching 12.376 billion yuan for the quarter, marking the twelfth consecutive quarter of triple-digit year-over-year growth. EBITA profit for the AI cloud and computing segment rose 133% year-over-year.

China Industry News

On August 20, the port of Murmansk in Russia held a welcoming ceremony for the first Chinese container ship to dock, celebrating the official launch of the port’s first container shipping line from China. This marks the formal commencement of regular cargo transport linking China’s coastal ports with Russia’s largest deep-water port in the Arctic Circle via the Arctic shipping route.

The second commercial satellite-based IoT license has been granted. The Ministry of Industry and Information Technology approved Zhejiang SpaceTime Daoyu Technology Co., Ltd. to conduct a two-year commercial trial of satellite-based IoT services. During this period, SpaceTime Universe will provide users with wide-coverage, low-power, and highly-reliable IoT connectivity services based on the “Geely Future Mobility Constellation (Phase I)”.

China has officially launched an innovation initiative for typical application scenarios of “AI + Transportation.” The Ministry of Transport has released the first batch of 41 key typical scenario construction guidelines covering 10 areas including intelligent driving, smart highways, intelligent railways, and smart aviation.

Shanghai has clarified its urban renewal and housing development tasks for the 15th Five-Year Plan, covering 28 items across seven aspects including housing improvement, housing security, and spatial revitalization. By the end of 2030, Shanghai plans to renovate 30 to 40 million square meters of old residential communities and add 25 to 28 million square meters of new commercial housing supply.

Wang Xingxing, Chairman of Unitree Technologies, stated at the 2026 World Robot Conference Forum that the biggest bottleneck in robotics is insufficient generalization capability of embodied intelligence. From a development cycle perspective, the industry could see a critical breakthrough within two to three years, or at the latest within five to ten years.

Fintech

U.S. President Trump met with top executives from the cryptocurrency industry at the White House and publicly urged Congress to pass the Digital Asset Market Structure Act, known as the “Clarity Act,” stating that the bill is critical for the United States to maintain its leadership in emerging technologies. However, the bill has stalled in the Senate due to controversy over moral clauses; as the November midterm elections approach, industry concerns are growing over a narrowing legislative window.

Corporate News & Updates

SK Hynix, in collaboration with researchers from the University of Virginia and other institutions, released a next-generation CPO roadmap — extending optical interconnects to memory interfaces to create an entirely new optics-centric architecture. SK Hynix and its labor union reached a provisional agreement: a 6.3% salary increase in 2026, with performance bonuses to be paid in a “40% cash + 60% stock” structure.

Micron Technology announced the establishment of the Micron Research Laboratory, committing $10 billion over the next decade to frontier areas including storage technology, advanced computing architectures, packaging processes, and semiconductor manufacturing. This investment is separate from the company’s previously announced total commitment of over $250 billion for U.S. manufacturing and R&D.

TSMC has completed development and validation of its 1.6nm-class A16 process and plans to begin mass production in the fourth quarter of this year. The A16 process targets the AI and high-performance computing markets. Compared to the enhanced 2nm process N2P, A16 delivers an 8%-10% performance improvement at the same power level and a 15%-20% power reduction at the same performance level, with chip density improved by 8%-10%.

According to sources, Broadcom is negotiating with a group of lenders to raise over $60 billion in debt financing for an AI chip transaction, which will benefit Anthropic PBC and other companies.

Harmony Intelligent Mobility unveiled its first technology-luxury off-road SUV, the Xiangjie G9, priced between 429,800 yuan and 549,800 yuan. The vehicle adopts an L3-level autonomous driving architecture and has received an L3-level autonomous driving road testing license. Huawei also released its first ultra-flat smartphone, the Pura X View, which will be the first to launch with HarmonyOS 7.

Global Macro & Policy

The Federal Reserve announced that Chair Warsh will deliver a keynote speech at the 2026 Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium hosted by the Kansas City Fed on August 28 at 10:00 a.m. Eastern Time (22:00 Beijing time).

St. Louis Fed President Musalem reiterated that he had originally hoped the Fed would raise rates at its July meeting to curb persistently high inflation. He believes that without an interest rate hike, the probability of inflation failing to return to the Fed’s 2% target within 18 months has increased.

Negotiations between Iran and Oman on establishing a joint mechanism for vessel transit through the Strait of Hormuz have reached their final stages. The Iran-Oman talks have frustrated Trump, who threatened that if Oman “obstructs” the U.S. reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, it would face U.S. bombing.

The Common App, the most widely used U.S. college application platform, released a report showing that the number of international applicants to U.S. universities this year decreased by nearly 16,000 compared to 2025, a year-over-year decline of about 10%, the largest drop in at least a decade. Application numbers from Asia and Africa both saw double-digit declines.

The Philadelphia Fed’s manufacturing index rose to 47.4 in August from a prior value of 41.4, the highest since 2021 and well above the market expectation of 24.8. The employment sub-index reached its highest level since April 2022, while prices, new orders, and shipments all declined compared to July levels.

U.S. initial jobless claims decreased by 6,000 to 206,000 last week, below economists’ forecast of 210,000. Continuing claims rose to 1.799 million, exceeding the market expectation of 1.79 million.

Affected by rising import costs for commodities such as crude oil, Japan recorded a trade deficit of 634.5 billion yen in July, marking the third consecutive month of deficit. Imports rose 27.8% year-over-year, the sixth consecutive month of growth, and the second consecutive month at a record high. Exports rose 23.2% year-over-year, marking the fifth consecutive month of accelerating growth.

Sources say UEFA, AFC, and CONCACAF are discussing a motion to initiate a vote of no confidence in FIFA President Infantino to seek his removal. Infantino plans to seek re-election and still retains support from some FIFA member associations, including those from the African Football Confederation.

Global Equity Markets

U.S. major indices closed lower: the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1.32% to 52,759.21, the S&P 500 dropped 0.87% to 7,641.16, and the Nasdaq Composite declined 1% to 26,067.17. Walmart fell over 9%, and Boeing dropped more than 3%, leading the Dow declines. Storage and optical communications sectors strengthened; SK Hynix rose over 4%, and Micron Technology gained nearly 4%. The Wind US Magnificent Seven Index fell 1.04%, with Amazon down over 2% and Apple off more than 1.5%. SpaceX fell over 4%. The Nasdaq Golden Dragon China Index dropped 1.15%, with Kingsoft Cloud down over 7% and Atour down more than 7%.

European major indices closed mixed: Germany’s DAX fell 0.42% to 25,983.04, France’s CAC 40 declined 0.57% to 8,453.09, and the UK’s FTSE 100 rose 0.04% to 10,748.16. Escalating U.S.-Iran tensions pushed Brent crude above $93, and the U.S. Treasury’s expanded long-term bond buyback program triggered bond market volatility, pressuring German and French equities into consecutive declines.

South Korea’s KOSPI surged 5.89% to close at 6,852.58, triggering a circuit breaker for program trading during the session. The Nikkei 225 rose 1.36% to 66,216.79. AI-related stocks rose collectively: SK Hynix jumped 12.73%, Samsung Electronics gained 9.49%, and Kioxia rose 6%. India’s SENSEX 30 rose 0.82% to 77,537.72.

The Bank of Korea reported that, driven by gains in domestic equities, foreign investors’ financial holdings in South Korea recorded the largest quarterly increase on record in the second quarter, reaching a new high. As of end-June, the total stock of foreign investment reached $3.02 trillion, up $891.2 billion from three months earlier.

Samsung Electronics plans to finalize and announce a shareholder return plan totaling over 100 trillion won. The company intends to allocate 50% of its free cash flow to shareholder returns, with measures expected to focus primarily on cash dividends. Additionally, Samsung will continue to consider supplementary shareholder return measures based on cash flow and profitability.

Anthropic expects its IPO size to reach at least the record level set by SpaceX, potentially even higher. Sources indicate that Anthropic is currently analyzing data and preparing to publicly file IPO documents as early as the end of this month.

Walmart reported second-quarter revenue of $187.94 billion, up 5.9% year-over-year, and adjusted EPS of $0.81, both exceeding market expectations. The company raised its full-year net sales growth forecast to 4%-5% and increased its adjusted EPS guidance to $2.80–$2.87. U.S. comparable store sales rose 2.6% year-over-year, the slowest pace in over six years.

Bonds

China’s interbank bond market remained largely volatile, with short-term bonds performing well while 30-year government bonds weakened. Futures contracts for government bonds declined across the board; the main 30-year contract closed down 0.24%. The interbank market liquidity remained stable and slightly loose; the PBOC continued zero operation on seven-day reverse repos, net draining 327.4 billion yuan for the day.

St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said recent bond market sell-offs were primarily driven by increased government borrowing and rising financing demand from AI infrastructure, not by market doubts about the Fed’s credibility. Over recent weeks, investors have continued to sell U.S. Treasuries, pushing the 30-year Treasury yield to its highest level since 2007.

U.S. Treasury yields rose across the board: the 2-year yield rose 1.67 basis points to 4.177%, the 3-year yield rose 3.09 basis points to 4.264%, the 5-year yield rose 4.43 basis points to 4.385%, the 10-year yield rose 5.94 basis points to 4.702%, and the 30-year yield rose 5.55 basis points to 5.247%.

Commodities

U.S. crude oil futures rose 2.16% to $86.21 per barrel; Brent crude futures climbed 1.77% to $93.24 per barrel. Ongoing geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, a sharp decline in crude oil transit through the Strait of Hormuz, and supply disruption fears have pushed up risk premiums; Angola plans to reduce October oil shipments, tightening supply expectations; U.S. distillate inventories fell to a one-month low, and refined product markets remain resilient, driving crude prices higher.

International precious metals futures generally rose: COMEX gold futures rose 0.66% to $4,575.10 per ounce; COMEX silver futures surged 3.50% to $68.13 per ounce. Heightened geopolitical uncertainty, weakening dollar stability, and declining dollar strength, combined with rising safe-haven demand and a reevaluation of gold’s strategic value amid de-dollarization trends, supported precious metal gains.

London base metals traded mixed: LME zinc rose 1.07% to $3,748.0 per ton, LME lead gained 0.64% to $1,899.5 per ton, LME tin rose 0.54% to $55,850.0 per ton, LME copper fell 0.06% to $14,041.5 per ton, LME nickel dropped 0.98% to $16,945.0 per ton, and LME aluminum declined 1.30% to $3,185.5 per ton.

OPEC forecasts that global natural gas demand will increase to over 91 million barrels of oil equivalent per day by 2050, up by more than 19 million barrels of oil equivalent per day from 2025. Natural gas will further solidify its long-term position in the global primary energy mix, largely replacing coal and supporting intermittent renewable energy in power generation.

Due to mutual attacks on ports and cargo ships by Russia and Ukraine, grain exports from both countries in the Black Sea and Azov Sea regions have nearly halted, with export capacity losses exceeding 97%. Global wheat prices have risen approximately 6.5% since August and are about 30% higher than the same period last year.

Russia’s central bank data showed that as of August 1, its gold reserves stood at 73.2 million ounces, down 1.6 million ounces from the start of the year and the lowest level since January 2020. In the first seven months of this year, the value of Russia’s central bank gold reserves declined cumulatively by $33.7 billion.

FX & Currency Markets

On Thursday, the onshore yuan closed at 6.7239 per U.S. dollar at 16:30, up 138 basis points from the previous trading day, reaching its highest level since early February 2023; the night session closed at 6.7260. The PBOC’s yuan midpoint was set at 6.7808, up 46 basis points from the previous day, marking a new high since February 2023.

At the close of New York trading, the U.S. dollar index rose 0.07% to 98.87; non-U.S. currencies were mixed: the euro rose 0.01% to 1.1679 against the dollar, the pound rose 0.18% to 1.3631, the Australian dollar fell 0.17% to 0.7113, the dollar rose 0.58% to 159.0680 against the yen, the dollar fell 0.13% to 1.3790 against the Canadian dollar, the dollar rose 0.41% to 0.8004 against the Swiss franc, and the offshore yuan rose 56 basis points to 6.7254 against the dollar.

4. Community Radio Faces Funding Shortfalls in Northeast
In the age of corporate-dominated media, Community Radio (CR) plays a crucial role in creating an inclusive space for communities living in remote and border regions to share their traditional knowledge and rich culture and access information about various development initiatives through participatory CR programmes. With 98% international borders and many smaller communities living in far-flung areas with poor connectivity, CR is an ideal community-driven grassroots communication platform for the region. However, official data shows that the funds intended to support the Community Radio (CR) movement in the region are not being used effectively, which highlights serious issues within institutions and systems that leave communities in need of reliable communication isolated. The creation of a new CR station in the area is not progressing, even though the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Communications and Information Technology recommended having at least one CR in each district, highlighting serious issues in planning, building capacity, and carrying out administrative tasks. The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting has told the parliamentary panel about several steps taken to improve the Community Radio (CR) movement in the region, which include activities to raise awareness specific to each state, ensuring that various activities of the scheme are done on time, engaging with stakeholders, informing ’eligible organisations, and providing training and capacity building. The budget for expanding CR in the area remains unused; the ongoing lack of use of funds from different schemes and projects shows a long-standing problem with administration. The committee observed an alarming trend of under-utilisation of funds for three successive financial years: 2O22- 23, 2O24-25 and 2O25-26. The ministry, however, attributes the gap to the receipt of a limited number of proposals from the region, among other reasons. This calls for demand-side interventions through intensification of the awareness of the CR movement among communities, educational institutions, NGOs and other eligible organisations in the region. Ensuring time-ly financial assistance and upgrading technical infrastructure to improve signal quality and reach in remote and tribal areas recommended by the parliamentary panel remains essential to see things moving in the right direction and gain pace. The ’Revised Guideline for setting up Community Radio Stations (CRS) in India’ issued in 2O24 states that any organisation wanting to create a CRS must be a not-for-profit group with at least three years of experience serving the community; the CRS must be designed to serve the local area it covers; and its ownership and management must reflect the community it serves. The guidelines also control what CRS can broadcast and require that programme production focus more on important topics like development, agriculture, health, education, the environment, social welfare, community development, and culture that are relevant to the local area. A key policy formulated by the central government regarding CRS permits them to broadcast public announcements about civic amenities, natural calamities, health alerts, and other information provided by the local administration, which is strategically relevant for the region. According to an official release issued by the Press Information Bureau, the Ministry urged the Chief Secretaries and the Administrative Secretaries of the Departments of Revenue and Disaster Management, as well as the concerned States, to utilise this effective medium for disseminating disaster-related information and to identify and promote the establishment of new CRSs in those areas. This policy promotes the use of CRS for disaster communication, emphasising the Northeast as the region most suitable for both disaster communication and the expansion of the CR network. Since the Central Sector Scheme, which helps set up CRS, has been approved to continue from 2O26-27 to 2O3O-3l with a budget of Rs. 5O crore, the Northeastern states should seize this opportunity and support the Ministry in expanding the CR network in the area. The scheme provides for financial assistance for procurement or replacement of equipment required for setting up and operation of CRS, including backup power equipment such as UPS, generator sets and solar power systems to ensure continuity of broadcasting during emergencies; and also provides for an emergency grant of Rs. ll.5O lakh to operational CRS in the event of natural disasters such as floods, lightning, earthquakes, etc. Given the region’s high vulnerability to natural disasters such as floods, landslides, and earthquakes, establishing new CRS in uncovered areas is not only a communication necessity but also a crucial requirement for disaster risk reduction. By organising programmes where communities share their traditional knowledge about being ready for disasters and experts provide scientific advice on early warnings and proven practices, CRS can help communities become better prepared for disasters and improve their ability to recover. As the impact of climate change deepens disaster crises in the region, expanding CR networks has become an urgent communication priority rather than just a routine developmental intervention.
Why it matters: Critical gap in disaster resilience communication for border regions.
Key detail: Despite parliamentary recommendations for district-level CR stations, funds remain unutilized due to administrative bottlenecks, leaving remote communities isolated during floods and landslides.
Source: Sentinel
Next step: Follow up with Ministry of I&B on revised guideline implementation timelines.

Statement : Shutting down Telegram is a band aid solution and is a disproportionate answer to exam fraud

The Internet Freedom Foundation objects to the directions announced today in the National Testing Agency's press release on action against the Telegram platform. On the NTA's recommendation, the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology has, under Section 69A of the Information Technology Act, 2000, restricted access to the whole of Telegram in India until 22 June 2026, and has separately ordered the platform to switch off message-editing for every Indian user until 30 June 2026. This is a blunt, nationwide measure aimed at the conduct of rampant fraud rackets, and on the Government's own admission is constitutionally incompatible.

At the outset it is important to note that Section 69A and the Blocking Rules of 2009 framed under it allow the Government to block access to specific “information” on a computer resource. They do not extend to switching off an entire intermediary, still less to ordering a company to redesign its product by removing a feature for a whole country. In Shreya Singhal v Union of India, the Supreme Court upheld Section 69A because it is narrow and hedged with procedural safeguards. Reading it to authorise shutting down a platform that lakhs use is an overbroad restriction by the NTAs own admission. For the message-editing direction the release identifies no source of power at all. If one exists, the order must say so.

The release argues against itself

A restriction on access has to be the least intrusive measure that achieves its aim as per the constitutional test of proportionality laid down in Justice K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (2017) and applied in Anuradha Bhasin v. Union of India (2020). The NTA's own narration shows the block fails its nodal agency, the release says, “has secured the prompt take-down of a substantial number of Telegram channels, groups and bots”, and this targeted work “is the reason the harm caused by these rackets has been contained to the extent it has”. If channel level takedown contained the harm, the case for a blanket block collapses and hence the Government has reached for a heavier tool while conceding that a lighter one was working. The collateral cost sits on the record too as noted in the press release. The block, the NTA accepts, “affects lakhs of citizens who use the Telegram platform for legitimate personal, educational, professional and informational purposes”. The release also says there is "no such paper available outside the secured examination chain" and that “the security of the examination is unaffected by the action taken”. If the exam is secure and no leak exists, what is being suppressed is rumour, and rumour cannot justify closing a platform when specific blocking and criminal prosecution remain available.

Students use of Telegram

The block of telegram is reactive and ineffective and will punish ordinary users instead of addressing the systemic source of exam leaks. This blocking comes in the final days of NEET preparation, when thousands of students depend on Telegram for study groups, doubt-clearing, and shared resources. Also, it is important to consider that the source of exam papers leak will occur from inside the system, among insiders and across the printing and logistics chain, with the platform being the most downstream channel for distribution. Hence, switching off Telegram, is merely a deflection from the repeated failures that will continue while media attention is directed towards this Telegram ban.

Lack of transparency

At present only a press release from the NTA has been provided, which recommended the block but the reasoned order of MeitY, the authority that issued it, has not been released. The Anuradha Bhasin decision requires that orders restricting access be published so they can be tested in court. Here the order, and the reasoning of the committee behind it, stay out of view, and we do not know whether Telegram was heard at all. An announcement of a block is no substitute for an order the affected party can challenge.
Blunt to enforce and very easy to evade
Usually, app-level blocks run through IS-level DNS and IP filtering. They are over inclusive, sweeping in lawful use, yet simple to evade as a determined exam leak racket moves to a VPN or a mirror within minutes while ordinary users lose the service for a week.

We ask the Government to:

1) Publish the MeitY Section 69A order and the NTA recommendation behind it, with reasons;
2) State the legal basis for the message editing direction, or withdraw it;
3) Confirm whether Telegram was given a hearing under the Blocking Rules, and place the committee's record before any court that hears a challenge; and
4) Lift the platform-wide restriction and rely on the targeted takedowns the NTA itself credits with containing the harm.

We emphasise that the NEET (UG) 2026 re-examination is worth protecting and it concerns the future of lakhs of aspirants. It requires securing the entire process of examination rather than reaching for purported band aid solutions that instead cause more harm. The State cannot switch off a service used by lakhs to answer the wrongdoing of a few, and cannot do it through an order no one affected is allowed to read. On its own facts, the Government has done both.

New Delhi, 16 June 2026.

The central question raised here is simple but fundamental: Why does India’s Prime Minister so rarely face an open press conference where journalists can ask unscripted questions?

The video argues that this is not merely about one politician's communication style. It is about whether the country's most powerful elected representative is willing to face independent scrutiny.

That question has acquired fresh significance after U.S. Ambassador Sergio Gor said that, ahead of Narendra Modi's June 17, 2026 meeting with Donald Trump at the G7 in France, India's side had requested that media be present but that there be no questions. Gor said Trump initially agreed, but subsequently invited questions, turning the interaction into what he described as a roughly 45-minute press conference. 

The accompanying material makes the same core argument: a democracy cannot be healthy if journalists are present only to listen, but not to question. 

COMMENTARY

A Prime Minister does not owe journalists obedience.

But a democracy owes its citizens answers.

And journalists are one of the mechanisms through which citizens ask those questions.

That is why the issue of press conferences is not a trivial obsession with television cameras.

A prepared interview allows the interviewer to know the subject.

A press conference allows the public's questions to enter the room.

They can be inconvenient.

They can be uncomfortable.

They can expose contradictions.

That is precisely why they matter.

The recent revelation about the Modi–Trump meeting makes the question even sharper.

According to the U.S. ambassador's account, India's preference was for media access without questions. The Indian government has characterised such discussions as normal arrangements for VVIP appearances. 

Fine.

Then let us ask the democratic question without partisan exaggeration:

Why should any democratic government be uncomfortable with questions?

If the Prime Minister has strong answers, questions provide an opportunity to demonstrate them.

If the government's policies are defensible, scrutiny strengthens their credibility.

If criticism is unfair, a public answer can expose it.

But when questioning itself becomes something to be managed, restricted or avoided, citizens are left with a dangerous imbalance:

Power gets to speak.
The public gets to listen.
And accountability gets postponed.

That is not the ideal of a free press.

A journalist's job is not to protect the image of the Prime Minister.

It is not to protect the opposition either.

It is to question power on behalf of the public.

And this principle must apply regardless of who occupies the Prime Minister's office.

Today Modi.

Tomorrow someone else.

The democratic standard must remain the same.

No leader should be above questions.

India does not need a Prime Minister who is merely excellent at delivering speeches.

India needs a Prime Minister confident enough to sit before journalists and say:

“Ask me anything.”

Because the real test of political confidence is not how loudly power speaks.

It is how calmly power answers.

— Reflection: A leader surrounded by applause may feel powerful. A leader willing to sit before uncomfortable questions is demonstrating something far more valuable—democratic confidence.

CREDIT

Credit to Ravish Kumar for raising the larger question of press freedom, journalistic questioning and political accountability, and to the reporting around U.S. Ambassador Sergio Gor's account of the Modi–Trump G7 interaction.

WHEN NEWS STOPS REPORTING POWER AND STARTS CELEBRATING IT

A former NDTV journalist describes a dramatic transformation in newsroom culture after the channel was acquired by the Adani Group: editors leaving, stories allegedly being blocked, government responses taking precedence over victims and experts, and government events increasingly being presented as celebrations rather than reported neutrally.

This is what happens when journalism forgets its first responsibility.

A newsroom is not supposed to be a government’s publicity department.

Its job is to question power, scrutinise claims, amplify the voices of those affected and tell citizens what those in power may not want them to know.

When a story begins with what the government says instead of what happened to the victim, journalism has already changed its priorities.

When a government event becomes a carnival on television, the boundary between reporting and propaganda begins to disappear.

And when ownership structures create a chain of influence — from proprietor to editor to newsroom desk — journalists may eventually begin censoring themselves before anyone even has to issue an order.

That is perhaps the most dangerous form of censorship:

the censorship that becomes instinctive.

“India on top.”
“What a moment.”
“Such a great achievement.”

These may sound like harmless television phrases.

But journalism becomes propaganda when celebration replaces scrutiny.

A democracy needs media that can make governments uncomfortable.

Because when journalists stop asking difficult questions, citizens are left with spectacle instead of information.

And without an informed citizenry, democracy becomes little more than a performance.

Journalism must report power — not perform for it.

1943 Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose's Rare Speech From Tokyo

Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose’s famous radio broadcast from Tokyo on 21 June 1943, which marked a massive turning point in India's armed struggle for independence. Following a perilous journey from Germany via a submarine, Netaji arrived in Japan to take control of the Indian National Army (INA) and broadcasted this call to action directly to the people of India.

The original audio of this rare address has been preserved and released by national archives like the Prasar Bharati Central Archives, as well as historical repositories on Internet Archive.

Netaji strongly criticised Anglo-American war propaganda. He explicitly mocked British military claims on the Indo-Burma frontier, pointing out how their forces retreated as soon as counter-offensives began.

He firmly stated that Indian citizens would never compromise with British imperialism, equating compromise to accepting permanent slavery.

He announced his presence in East Asia to organize an armed rebellion from outside Indian borders, calling upon all freedom-loving Indians to prepare for the ultimate sacrifice.

Netaji underscored that Indian liberty was closely linked with the total overthrow of Anglo-American imperialism across East.

June 19, 1943 Press Conference: Two days before his broadcast, Netaji held an official press conference in Tokyo. He explained the genuine sentiments of Indians and highlighted the civilizational bonds between India and Japan.

November 1943 Greater East Asia Conference: Netaji attended this summit alongside Japan's Prime Minister Hideki Tojo. During this historic gathering, he successfully secured the sovereignty of the Provisional Government of Azad Hind and negotiated the handover of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands back to India.

IFF’s Statement on the Blocking of X Account of the Cockroach Janta Party

22 May 2026

On May 21, 2026, the X (formerly Twitter) handle of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) (@CJP_2029) was withheld in India under Section 69A of the Information Technology Act, 2000. IFF strongly condemns the blocking of the CJP’s X handle as a blatant misuse of State power and an arbitrary and disproportionate attempt to stifle freedom of speech and expression, a fundamental right guaranteed under Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution of India.

According to reporting by The Indian Express on May 22, 2026, the blocking directions were issued on the basis of inputs from the Intelligence Bureau citing threat to the sovereignty of India, jeopardizing national security and the fact that the account was gaining traction among young people. Section 69A of the IT Act, 2000, empowers the Central government to direct any Government agency or intermediary to block public access to information in the “interest of sovereignty and integrity of India, defence of India, security of the State, friendly relations with foreign States or public order or for preventing incitement to the commission of any cognizable offence”. While Section 69A of the IT Act, 2000 permits blocking on limited grounds, these grounds cannot be vague and speculative. Political commentary and criticism of public institutions are protected forms of speech under the Indian Constitution. The popularity of the account or the fact that the account mobilised young people through political expression cannot by itself be treated as a threat to national security.

The Indian Express’s report mentions that “blocking orders are issued under a confidential framework” which is deeply concerning. We remind the Union Government that the Supreme Court of India upheld Section 69A of the IT Act, 2000 in Shreya Singhal v. Union of India (2015) on the basis that it is a narrowly drawn provision with several safeguards in place, including written reasoning for the blocking that is subject to legal challenge. State censorship like the blocking of CJP’s X account propagates opacity and provides affected users with no options for redressal, thereby effectively defeating these safeguards. IFF calls on the Union government to ensure timely notices are provided to affected users along with clear grounds and avenues for remedy.

IFF has previously explained how users whose constitutional rights are being infringed upon by the State can seek restoration of their blocked content. If you are an Indian social media user or journalist whose content has been blocked due to a government order, please write to us at legal@internetfreedom.in.

A Delhi High Court order has once again had to remind the Grievance Appellate Committee to follow the timeline already prescribed under the IT Rules, 2021. On 20 August 2026, the Court directed the GAC to decide the appeal of content creator Riya, whose Instagram account #riaspeaks has over five lakh followers, within 30 days. Her appeal had already been pending for more than 42 days. (1/7)
Read More: https://t.co/26gA6SeMe0

The GAC is particularly important because it is supposed to provide users with an appellate remedy against intermediary decisions, including arbitrary or permanent account bans. Yet when an appeal itself remains pending beyond the prescribed period, a creator can be left with no meaningful remedy except approaching a High Court. The burden then falls on users and the judiciary alike. (6/7)

IFF had earlier suggested increasing the number of GACs to deal with the growing volume of appeals and making GAC orders publicly accessible, given the quasi-adjudicatory nature of their work. Neither has happened. We are assisting Riya through the appeal process and will continue to monitor the matter. (7/7)
